verdict: Leads are down this week; heating campaigns are launching now to reverse it.
narrative: Over the last 28 days you received 34 leads at an average cost of $43.86 per lead, but the most recent 7 days showed a 38.89% drop in leads alongside a 19.91% rise in cost per lead — a combination that points to a structural gap, not just a slow week. Google Ads absorbed $969.86 of the 28-day spend yet all 34 tracked leads came through Meta, meaning Google spend has not been converting at the expected rate. The core reason is that heating-season campaigns — due live October 1 — are overdue and being launched now, and Local Services Ads are being re-enabled this week to add a second paid lead source heading into peak heating demand. On the organic side, your Google Business Profile activity surged 33% week-over-week with 144 actions and 21 calls across both profiles, confirming that local intent is real and that the paid channels, once properly activated, have demand to capture.

highlights.phrase: leads received in the last 28 days, all attributed to Meta ads
average cost per lead this period, up roughly 20% in the most recent week
Google Business Profile actions this period, up 33% week-over-week

watch_item.issue: Google Ads spend is running at roughly half its prior pace and heating campaigns have not yet been live for the season, leaving paid lead volume well below where it should be entering November.
watch_item.fix: Heating campaigns and Local Services Ads are being activated this week, and budget is scheduled to be restored to full pace by October 31.
